This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondent under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12%
p.a.
2.

The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 04.06.2024 at about 10.40 a.m. Baby had been proceeding as a pillion rider on Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-ET-1978 rode by her father i.e., petitioner No.2 on Mysore - Bengaluru Service Road, near Siri Convention Hall, Kaniminike Village,
Kengeri Hobli, SCCH 5 Bengaluru, at that time, a BMTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-F-8897 being driven by its driver came from back side at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said scooter and drag to some distance and then the wheel of the Bus ran over the deceased and dashed to another Scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-51-EY-5241.Due to the impact,BabyK. was died on the spot and petitioner No.2 sustained grievous injuries and scooter also damaged extensively.

Immediately after the accident, body of the deceased was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical College Hospital, Kengeri, wherein postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to the petitioners, who spent Rs.1,00,000/-
towards funeral and other incidental expenses.

3. At the time of accident, deceased/Baby K. was aged about 18 years, she was student and going to admission to B.E., at the time of accident and she also SCCH 5 doing tailoring work and earning more than Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to sudden and untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have lost their daughter and her love and affection, they are undergoing mental shock, agony and financial loss.
With regard to accident, crime No.189/2024 is registered against the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-01-F-8897 before the Kumbalagudu Police.
Respondent was the owner and internal insurer of the BMTC is liable to pay compensation.
So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement and submitted that, petition is bad for mis-joinder and non- joinder of parties.

Further submitted that,
rider of the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-ET-1978 was wholly and solely responsible for the accident.
Further denied SCCH 5 rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the BMTC.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.

Respondent submitted that,
compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5.

Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:

sentences.text: 1. Whether Petitioner proves that, deceased Baby, D/o. Keshava Murthy died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 04.06.2024 at about 10.40 p.m. near Siri Convention Hall, Kaniminike Village, Mysore - Bengaluru Service Road, Kengeri, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-F-8897 dashed against the deceased and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
SCCH 5 3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.2/ father of the deceased examined as PW-1 and exhibited 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.

On the other hand, driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-01-F- 8897 has deposed his evidence as RW-1.
7.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this SCCH 5 regard he has exhibited copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of mahazar as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch as Ex.P.4, copy of inquest as Ex.P.5, copy of Sec.133 notice as Ex.P.6, copy of reply as Ex.P.7, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.8, copy of P.M.Report as Ex.P.9 and copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.10.
9.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those were marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 04.06.2024 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-01-F-8897 has deposed as RW-1 and stated that the he was driving the bus slowly and cautiously on the left side of road and it is by the rash and negligent driving of rider of two wheeler accident occured.
Except oral evidence of R.W-1 nothing is put forth to discard the SCCH 5 contents of Ex.P.10.During
the cross examination of R.W- 1
it is elicited that he has not challenged the charge sheet filed against him.

It is admitted by Shivamma vs B.M.T.C on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113714047/
3 respondent that they granted interim compensation of Rs.25,000/-.If at all the accident is not due to rash and negligent driving of driver of bus what made the respondent to pay interim compensation.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, it is proved by the petitioner about death of Baby K due to the accident occurred on 04.06.2024 at about 10.40 a.m. when she was riding as a pillion rider on scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-ET-1978 on Mysore - Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital Service Road, near Siri Convention Hall, Kaniminike Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru City.
11. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-01-F-8897.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence SCCH 5 and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioner, deceased/Baby K. was aged about 18 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, petitioner has produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.11, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 02.10.2006,
the alleged accident was occurred in the year 04.06.2024.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.11, age of the deceased is considered about 18 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: SCCH 5 13.
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was a student and was going to admission to B.E. at the time of accident and she was also doing tailoring work, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The petitioner not produced any document to show that deceased was B.E student.
Hence monthly income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.16,500/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.
14. Further petitioners are the parents of the deceased/ Baby K.

To prove the said fact, PW-1 has produced copy of aadhar card of petitioner No.1 and 2 which are marked as Ex.P.11, it reveals that,
they are the legal representatives of Baby K.
15.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased was bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so SCCH 5 that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

16. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

Further he is also entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 24,94,800-00 2. Loss of filial consortium 40,000-00 3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 SCCH 5 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 25,64,800-00 20.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,64,800/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
21.

In the case on hand, respondent being the R.C.Owner and internal insurer of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-01-F-8897 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

5 The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,64,800/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Sixty Four Thousand Eight Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 50:50 in the award amount.

The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.

The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH 5 Draw award accordingly.
